narrative.northStar: The Post Office on the Desktop
narrative.overview:
Dak is a macOS mail client whose post is agent work. It is built to disappear into the system it runs on: a translucent source-list sidebar, a 52px unified toolbar with the traffic lights centred in it, San Francisco type, neutral greys, and hairlines instead of cards. Nothing about it reads as a web dashboard. The agent's explanation and the conversation sit beside the thing under review, and the reading surface stays quiet so the PR or the document is what you look at.

The one loud thing is India Post red, and it is rationed. It marks the primary action, the current selection inside the content, and what is waiting on you. Everything else is ink on grey. The post-office identity lives in the name (डाक, "the post"), in that red, and in the app icon, an India Post pillar box with a letter going into its slot; the screens themselves carry no stamps, textures or postal decoration.

Density is a Mac app's, not a website's: a 13px base, 28px controls, 6px corners, tight rows. Reading surfaces open up (14 to 14.5px at 1.6 line height in a 700 to 720px column) because reading is the job. Light and dark follow the system appearance through one set of tokens.
keyCharacteristics: Native shell first: hidden title, full-size content, translucent sidebar material, native menus, Dock badge, menu bar count, notifications.
One accent, rationed: India Post red for the primary action, in-content selection and "waiting on you".
One ink for every agent: a tool logo or an initial, never a per-agent colour.
Hairlines and tonal washes for structure; shadows only on things that float.
System type only: SF Pro for UI and reading, SF Mono for code.
One icon family (Phosphor regular) and real tool logos from Simple Icons, all in currentColor.

rules.name: The Rationed Red Rule
rules.body: India Post red means one of three things: this is the primary action, this is what you have selected inside the content, or this is waiting on you. One red-filled button per view. If red is doing something else, it is wrong.

rules.name: The Native Selection Rule
rules.body: The sidebar selects like a Mac source list, in neutral grey (`selection-grey`). Red tint is for selection inside the reading surface (a chapter, a line range, a paragraph, a pick), where it ties the selection to what you are commenting on.

rules.name: The One Ink Rule
rules.body: Agents never get colours of their own. Every agent is drawn in `ink-secondary` on `hairline-soft`, distinguished by its tool's logo or its initial.

rules.name: The System Voice Rule
rules.body: Only the system stacks. No web font is loaded, and none should be.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every label, button and heading is sentence case. No uppercase labels, no letter-spaced small caps.

rules.name: The Beside Rule
rules.body: The conversation sits beside the thing under review, never above it or in a modal. At desktop widths both are always visible.

rules.name: The Hairlines Not Cards Rule
rules.body: Lists, threads, settings and document comments are rows divided by hairlines. A box with a shadow means it floats; nothing that sits in the flow gets one.

dos: **Do** keep exactly one red-filled button per view, on the action that sends or advances.
**Do** draw every agent with the agent mark: tool logo or initial, `ink-secondary` on `hairline-soft`.
**Do** use Phosphor regular icons at 16px (17px in icon buttons, 14px in buttons, 13px in chips), in currentColor.
**Do** separate rows with 1px hairlines and reserve the Float shadow for the composer, open editors, popovers and toasts.
**Do** write every label in sentence case and every timestamp and count with tabular figures.
**Do** give every new colour a dark value in the `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block, and lift red to the brighter dark accent there.
**Do** keep the conversation beside the review at desktop widths.
donts: **Don't** give an agent its own colour, coloured avatar or coloured pill.
**Don't** use India Post red for decoration, success, headings or anything not primary, selected or waiting on you.
**Don't** use post yellow anywhere in the interface; it lives in the icon.
**Don't** load a web font or use a non-system face.
**Don't** wrap list content in shadowed cards or build a dashboard of tiles.
**Don't** add a second icon family or brand marks whose licence does not allow it.
